analysis.title: Tech capitulation, anti-AI euphoria and the rush to safety
key_insights: NDX is back near its long-term trendline after another round of selling. It is well below the 200-day moving average, momentum is poor, and the 21-day average is crossing below the 200-day.

Goldman prime brokerage data shows US technology long/short positioning at its lowest since records began in 2016. The selling has moved from long liquidation and de-grossing to outright short building.
CTAs have sold technology aggressively, with Nasdaq positioning back near maximum short levels. The note says this leaves the door open for a potentially violent squeeze.
The BofA Fund Manager Survey shows tech allocations at their lowest since June 2006.
Nvidia is down 35% from its October peak despite a large upward revision to long-term earnings expectations. DB's Jim Reid notes NVDA trades at roughly 6x projected 2031 earnings.
Goldman downgraded Taiwan from Overweight to Market Weight and cut its TAIEX target from 57,500 to 50,000. The new end-2027 target still implies almost 20% upside.
Goldman projects Taiwan EPS growth of 32% in 2027 and 25% in 2028, but cut its target forward P/E to 14x, leaving less room for multiple expansion.
Taiwan technology exports continue to grow strongly while the equity market has stopped responding. Goldman says positioning, valuations and the semiconductor cycle now dominate price action.
Goldman highlights record leveraged-ETF exposure and elevated margin balances in Taiwan. This leaves equities exposed to forced selling through leveraged ETF rebalancing and margin calls.

MSCI India has outperformed MSCI EM by 13.7% so far this month, the strongest relative performance since May 2009. Goldman raised its 12-month NIFTY target to 28,500, citing domestic demand and low foreign ownership.

The note says India's short-term setup is stretched: foreign buying has accelerated and much of the index short covering is done. JPMorgan flags rising input costs, margin pressure, weaker rural prospects after a poor monsoon, and tighter monetary conditions.
India's rally has coincided with oil falling, continuing the inverse relationship between the two. Indian equities have now overshot the move in oil by a wide margin.

Goldman's Privorotsky highlights a large rerating in defensives. XLU has outperformed TLT by about 5 percentage points over 20 sessions, a 3-standard-deviation move, while nominal and real yields remain elevated.
The note reads the defensive rerating as the equity market pricing a growth scare that the bond market has not acknowledged.

sector_views.rationale: Goldman moved Taiwan from Overweight to Market Weight, citing valuation. EPS growth is strong but there is less room for multiple expansion.
Goldman remains constructive and raised its 12-month NIFTY target to 28,500, but the note and JPMorgan prefer rebuilding exposure on a consolidation rather than chasing.
Fund manager allocations are at their lowest since 2006 and hedge fund tech long/short positioning is at a record low. The note frames this as a squeeze setup, not a fundamental call.
Defensives have rerated sharply, with XLU outperforming TLT by about 5 points over 20 sessions. Goldman reads this as a growth scare being priced in equities.
